title: Slicing flat equivalence relations without changing their fppf quotient
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For $S$-schemes $V,R$, an equivalence relation $j=(s,t):R\to V\times_SV$ [def-pc-fibre-product] means that $j$ is injective on sections over every $S$-scheme $T$ and identifies $R(T)$ with an equivalence relation on $V(T)$. Write $V/R$ for the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site] of $T\mapsto V(T)/R(T)$. Assume $s,t$ are flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There exist $S$-schemes $V',R'$, an equivalence relation $(s',t'):R'\to V'\times_SV'$, and a morphism $g:V'\to V$ carrying $R'$ into $R$, such that the induced map $V'/R'\to V/R$ is an isomorphism of fppf sheaves and both $s',t'$ are flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 0489 (lemma-slice-equivalence-relation). The printed conclusion has R to U instead of R-prime to U-prime; the intended source and target are explicit in the proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-relation-cm-open] to obtain $W\subseteq V$ and $R_W=W\times_{V,t}R\times_{s,V}W$. The saturation $h_W$ is surjective, flat and locally finitely presented. Thus [lem-sfb-relation-restriction-quotient] gives $W/R_W\simeq V/R$. It remains to slice the Cohen--Macaulay relation on $W$; the final morphism to $V$ will be the composite through $W$.

For every finite type point $w\in W$, apply [lem-sfb-cm-relation-point-slice] to $(W,R_W)$: choose $g_w:A_w\to W$ and $a_w\in A_w$ with $g_w(a_w)=w$. Put $H_w=A_w\times_{g_w,W,t}R_W$ and $h_w=s\operatorname{pr}_{R_W}:H_w\to W$. Each $h_w$ is flat, locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite. The identity arrow at $w$ paired with $a_w$ gives a point of $H_w$ mapping to $w$.

source.place: Tag 0489 (lemma-slice-equivalence-relation), Step 2 and beginning of Step 3; Tag 04N0

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finite type points of $W$. Form $A=\coprod_{w\in I}A_w$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], with $g:A\to W$ induced by the $g_w$, and set $D=A\times_{g,W,t}R_W\times_{s,W,g}A$. For every test scheme $T$, its sections are triples $(a,r,b)$ with $t(r)=g(a)$ and $s(r)=g(b)$. For given $(b,a)$ there is at most one $r$; reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity follow from those of $R_W(T)$ by pulling back along $g$. Hence $D\rightrightarrows A$, with $s_D(a,r,b)=b$ and $t_D(a,r,b)=a$, is an equivalence relation carrying into $R_W$. This verification uses the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 0489 (lemma-slice-equivalence-relation), Step 3; restriction as in groupoids-lemma-restrict-relation

proof.text: The inverse images of the disjoint open components $A_w\subseteq A$ give $H=A\times_{g,W,t}R_W=\coprod_w H_w$ and $h=s\operatorname{pr}_{R_W}:H\to W$ restricts to $h_w$ on $H_w$. Thus $h$ is flat, locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite: any point is in one open component, where its stalk map is that of $h_w$, and affine neighbourhoods witnessing finite presentation and quasi-finiteness there remain affine open neighbourhoods in $H$. These are exactly the pointwise conditions in [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 0489 (lemma-slice-equivalence-relation), Step 3, coproduct of h_w; locality checked directly

proof.text: The scheme $D$ is $H\times_{h,W,g}A$ and $s_D:D\to A$ is the base change of $h$. Flatness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], local finite presentation from clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], and local quasi-finiteness from clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change]. Swapping $a,b$ and taking the unique reverse relation arrow gives an involution $D\simeq D$ exchanging $s_D$ and $t_D$; its square is the identity because relation arrows with fixed endpoints are unique. Thus both projections have all three properties.

source.place: Tag 0489 (lemma-slice-equivalence-relation), Step 3, displayed fibre-product formula and projection argument

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], the image $O=h(H)$ is open in $W$. Step 2 shows that $O$ contains every finite type point of $W$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-points-detect-open] to conclude $O=W$, so $h$ is surjective. Explicitly, a nonempty closed complement would contain a finite type point outside $O$, a contradiction. Therefore $\{h\}$ is an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]; no quasi-compactness or Jacobson hypothesis on $W$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0489 (lemma-slice-equivalence-relation), last paragraph, using the full conclusion of Tag 02J4 and openness from Tag 01UA

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relation-restriction-quotient] to $g:A\to W$ and the surjective flat locally finitely presented map $h$ of steps 4 and 6. It gives $A/D\simeq W/R_W$. Compose with the isomorphism of step 1 to obtain $A/D\simeq V/R$, induced by $A\xrightarrow{g}W\hookrightarrow V$. Take $V\prime=A$, $R\prime=D$. By construction $D$ carries into $R_W$ and then $R$, and step 5 supplies the required properties of both projections.

All constructions remain in the chosen universes [def-weil-size-convention]. The index $I$ is a subset of $|W|$, not a proper class; the individual affine slices are schemes in the scheme universe and their set-indexed disjoint union is the scheme of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The finite fibre products defining $H$ and $D$ lie in the same universe. Choose their representatives in the fixed larger-universe site skeleton. If $W$ is empty, $I,A,H,D$ are empty and the arguments above hold with vacuous local conditions and the empty covering of the empty scheme.

tool_uses.why: General existence and open components of arbitrary set-indexed scheme coproducts, needed for assembling local slices; no such geometric coproduct statement in this unit.
Only clause (2), preservation of locally quasi-finite morphisms in the Stacks sense under arbitrary base change, is used for the sliced projection; a generic scheme-theoretic permanence tool.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q142-e0e96cc63 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all three new nodes and every cited statement in full, against Stacks 0489 (bootstrap.tex lemma-slice-equivalence-relation), 0460 (lemma-make-CM), 04N0 (lemma-max-slice-quasi-finite) with 04MY, 02VH (lemma-quotient-groupoid-restrict), 045R (definition-CM) and 02J4 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points). The item statement is unchanged from the base and correctly fixes the source's R->U typo to R'->U'. New nodes: (1) flat-relation-cm-open is 0460 clauses (4) and (5) for an equivalence relation; h_W is s restricted to the open t^{-1}(W), so it is flat and locally finitely presented; the inline CM definition agrees with 045R. (2) cm-relation-point-slice is 04N0 clauses (2)-(4); its stabilizer hypothesis is automatic because the stabilizer of an equivalence relation is the identity V. (3) relation-restriction-quotient is 02VH for fppf with an arbitrary g, and the surjective flat lfp hypothesis on h is exactly an fppf covering. I tested all three on the trivial relation Delta_V and on V empty. None duplicates an existing node: lem-trf-etale-relation-restriction-quotient needs etale maps and surjective g, lem-trf-etale-relation-finding-opens needs flat g, the fppf-generator comparison needs etale g, and the CM-locus and CM-chart nodes concern a single morphism. Steps: step 2's point over w exists because a_w and e(w) have the same image; in step 5, D = H x_{h,W,g} A, so local quasi-finiteness follows from clause (2) of the separated/lqf base-change node alone; in step 6, image openness plus the same-unit 02J4 detector gives surjectivity; step 8 handles sizes and the empty case. Steps 3 and 4 are genuinely elementary. The declared tool_uses (scheme coproduct, Mathlib leaf; separated/lqf base change clause (2)) are generic and accepted. stmt_deps and proof_deps are consistent, there is no SGA citation, no cycle and no repair note. No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem exists_fppf_relation_slicing {S : Scheme.{u}} {V R : Over S} (s t : R ⟶ V) (hinj : ∀ T : Over S, Function.Injective (fun r : T ⟶ R ↦ (r ≫ s, r ≫ t))) (hrel : ∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) [Flat s.left] [Flat t.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation s.left] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation t.left] : ∃ (V' R' : Over S) (s' t' : R' ⟶ V') (g : V' ⟶ V) (r : R' ⟶ R) (F F' : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ F.obj) (η' : coequalizer (yoneda.map s') (yoneda.map t') ⟶ F'.obj) (e : F' ≅ F), (∀ T : Over S, Function.Injective (fun a : T ⟶ R' ↦ (a ≫ s', a ≫ t'))) ∧ (∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V' ↦ ∃ q : T ⟶ R', q ≫ s' = a ∧ q ≫ t' = b)) ∧ r ≫ s = s' ≫ g ∧ r ≫ t = t' ≫ g ∧ Flat s'.left ∧ Flat t'.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation s'.left ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation t'.left ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite s'.left ∧ Scheme.Hom.IsLocallyQuasiFinite t'.left ∧ (∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun k : F.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ k)) ∧ (∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun k : F'.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η' ≫ k)) ∧ (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s') (yoneda.map t') ≫ η') ≫ e.hom.hom = yoneda.map g ≫ (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η)
